To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we prove equivalence of the original infinite horizon discounted optimal stochastic control problem and a linear program over a probability space, under mild assumptions; (b) we prove that, under polynomial data and mild assumptions, the value function and an approximate optimal feedback can be approximated by solving a hierarchy of semidefinite programming problems.
we have proved equivalence of the original problem with an infinite-dimensional linear programming problem over a measure space.

we have shown how to approximate the value of the optimal control problem and the optimal feedback control by solving an infinite-dimensional linear programming problem and its finite-dimensional relaxations, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How to approximate the value functions of infinite horizon, discounted optimal control problems, and how to use the approximation to compute approximate optimal controllers?
a new approach to the solution of infinite horizon deterministic optimal control problems.
a new, more general, approach to the linear programming formulation of optimal control problems, which is based on dually equivalent infinite-dimensional linear programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a wide class of problems, the moment approach is the most efficient method for the design and analysis of approximate solutions to optimal control problems.
the linear programming approach is a very powerful tool for the analysis of infinite horizon optimal control problems.
the linear programming approach is not a panacea for the moment approach, but rather an alternative that is more amenable to numerical computation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the moment-sum-of-square approach is a promising tool for approximating optimal feedback controllers in deterministic continuous time infinite horizon problems.

, for the first time, we have shown that the linear program approach to deterministic infinite horizon discounted optimal problems is indeed equivalent to a linear program over an infinite dimensional measure space.
we have developed a novel approach to the infinite horizon discounted optimal stochastic control problems by relaxing it to a measure theoretic linear programming problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the linear programming approach can be used for problems that are more general than those considered so far in the literature, and that the moment approach can be used to approximate optimal solutions and feedback laws for problems that are not convex in the control.

the infinite-dimensional linear program provides an effective and robust tool for designing approximate optimal controllers for deterministic continuous time infinite horizon discounted control problems.
infinite horizon discounted optimal problems are well-posed and can be approximated efficiently using the moment approach.
